first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_misf.description: After the reconciliation only KXMLBRFI, KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN remain; the inputs mlb.f3_split and mlb.tto and the PA dataset still carry F3/F5-oriented content inherited from the earlier filing, and whether other inning strikes (innings 2-8) trade at all is unknown.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_misf.what_would_resolve: List the live KXMLBINNINGTOTAL/INNINGWIN strikes by inning and drop F-series inputs that serve no inning market.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_misf.classification_rationale: Records defect: mlb.f3_split, mlb.tto and the PA dataset still carry F3/F5 content from a superseded filing, so the input list of the archetype is wrong for KXMLBRFI, KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN.
first_inning_and_inning_markets#inn_misf.catalog_action: Edit first_inning_and_inning_markets: strip F3/F5-specific content from mlb.f3_split, mlb.tto and the PA dataset, keep only inputs serving RFI/INNINGTOTAL/INNINGWIN, and list live inning strikes from the series ledger.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_hrr_cha.description: KXMLBHRR (hits plus runs plus RBIs) is live here but only slot-level rbi_opportunity and run_scoring_opportunity exist; the lineup-neighbour on-base chain defined for the RBI archetype (pa_base_out_state_chain) is not available to this record, so the runs and RBI components are modelled more crudely than in the RBI archetype.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_hrr_cha.what_would_resolve: Share one base-out chain input between the hits and RBI archetypes once the catalog merge defines it, then compare HRR rung calibration with and without it.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_hrr_cha.classification_rationale: Missing interaction: KXMLBHRR's runs and RBI components lack the lineup-neighbour base-out chain (pa_base_out_state_chain) that the RBI archetype defines, so the hits record's input list is incomplete for HRR.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases#hits_hrr_cha.catalog_action: Define one shared pa_base_out_state_chain input and attach it to hitter_hits_and_total_bases for KXMLBHRR's runs/RBI legs, mirroring hitter_rbis_runs_sb.

hitter_home_runs#hr_opp_starter_change.description: The single-game HR ladder is conditional only on the hitter, so a scratch of the opposing starter does not trigger the fair-price branch, yet the only availability input is lineup_pit; the probable-pitcher change risk input defined in first5_markets is not available here and pitcher_hr_vulnerability is evaluated for the announced starter only.
hitter_home_runs#hr_opp_starter_change.what_would_resolve: Define a shared probable-pitcher-change input and evaluate pitcher_hr_vulnerability as a mixture over the announced and replacement starters.
hitter_home_runs#hr_opp_starter_change.classification_rationale: Missing input: the HR ladder evaluates pitcher_hr_vulnerability for the announced starter only and has no probable-pitcher-change input, although a scratch of the opposing starter does not trigger fair price.
hitter_home_runs#hr_opp_starter_change.catalog_action: Attach the shared probable-pitcher-change input (from first5_markets) to hitter_home_runs and redefine pitcher_hr_vulnerability as a mixture over announced and replacement starters.

hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_runs_scope.description: The archetype description includes runs scored, but no runs-scored series exists; only KXMLBRBI and KXMLBSB (one rung each, postseason games) were sampled, so other rungs, regular-season wording and postponement handling are unseen.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_runs_scope.what_would_resolve: Re-file KXMLBSB here or review it with the counting-specials record; check whether a runs-scored ladder exists.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_runs_scope.classification_rationale: Series/archetype mapping defect: the record's scope claims runs scored though no runs-scored series is filed, and only KXMLBRBI and KXMLBSB belong to it, so scope and inputs disagree with the filed series.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb#rbi_runs_scope.catalog_action: Revise hitter_rbis_runs_sb scope to KXMLBRBI and KXMLBSB, drop runs-scored inputs unless the series ledger shows a runs ladder, and confirm KXMLBSB filing versus counting specials.

offfield_markets#off_unstaged_inputs.description: New inputs defined for series that left this archetype (sale stage hazard, manager award score, esports rating, manager candidate signal) remain defined in this record for catalog consistency but are not staged; integration will still attach them to this archetype unless removed.
offfield_markets#off_unstaged_inputs.what_would_resolve: Detach those inputs from offfield_markets at integration or move them to the archetypes that now hold their series.
offfield_markets#off_unstaged_inputs.classification_rationale: Records defect: inputs for series that left offfield_markets (sale stage hazard, manager award score, esports rating, manager candidate signal) remain attached and would be integrated into the wrong archetype.
offfield_markets#off_unstaged_inputs.catalog_action: Detach sale-stage hazard, manager award score, esports rating and manager candidate signal from offfield_markets and attach each to the archetype now holding its series.

pitcher_outs#outs_hazard_naming.description: The starter exit-hazard object appears under three ids across sibling archetypes (leash/sp_workload, sp_hook_hazard_curve, exit_boundary_mass); duplicates in the catalog would be fitted separately and drift apart.
pitcher_outs#outs_hazard_naming.what_would_resolve: Define one shared hazard-model input and map the strikeout, outs and earned-run records to it.
pitcher_outs#outs_hazard_naming.classification_rationale: Definition defect: the starter exit hazard is defined three times (sp_workload/leash, sp_hook_hazard_curve, exit_boundary_mass) across sibling archetypes, which would be fitted separately and drift apart.
pitcher_outs#outs_hazard_naming.catalog_action: Author one shared starter exit-hazard input id and remap sp_workload, sp_hook_hazard_curve and exit_boundary_mass in pitcher_strikeouts, pitcher_outs and pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks to it.

pitcher_strikeouts#ks_talent_prior_gap.description: Pitcher-side talent rests on k_rates, pitch_type_whiff and a 120-BF half-life with no stuff-model or projection-system K% prior for arsenal changes, injury returns or rookies, exactly where pitch-level whiff samples are thinnest.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_talent_prior_gap.what_would_resolve: Add a stuff-quality or projection K% prior (e.g. ZiPS/Steamer or a pitch-model grade) and test it on pitchers with changed arsenals.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_talent_prior_gap.classification_rationale: Missing input: pitcher talent has no stuff-model or projection K% prior, so arsenal changes, injury returns and rookies have no defined information source where whiff samples are thinnest.
pitcher_strikeouts#ks_talent_prior_gap.catalog_action: Add a pitcher K% prior input to pitcher_strikeouts (pitch-model stuff grade or ZiPS/Steamer projection) with source and blending rule versus k_rates and pitch_type_whiff.

player_participation#pp_cba_lockout.description: Any 2027 KXMLBSTART, KXMLBSTARTER or KXMLBPITCH window depends on the CBA that expires Dec 1 2026; a lockout that cancels games would void or shrink the window (treatment unseen), and the labour input is defined in transactions (mlb.labor_stoppage_regime) and not staged here.
player_participation#pp_cba_lockout.what_would_resolve: Stage mlb.labor_stoppage_regime for 2027 windows and obtain the contract treatment of cancelled games.
player_participation#pp_cba_lockout.classification_rationale: Missing attachment: 2027 KXMLBSTART/STARTER/PITCH windows depend on mlb.labor_stoppage_regime, defined in transactions but not staged here. CBA expiry verified as 11:59 pm ET Dec 1 2026.
player_participation#pp_cba_lockout.catalog_action: Stage mlb.labor_stoppage_regime in player_participation for 2027 KXMLBSTART/STARTER/PITCH windows and record cancelled-game treatment as a contract dependency.

player_participation#pp_opp_starter_vint.description: Platoon-driven start decisions depend on the opposing probable starter's identity and hand and when it was announced, but no input carries them; platoon (a duplicate in other archetypes) only stands in for the hand.
player_participation#pp_opp_starter_vint.what_would_resolve: Define an opposing-probable-starter input with announcement timestamp and use it in the manager-decision stage.
player_participation#pp_opp_starter_vint.classification_rationale: Missing input: platoon start decisions depend on the opposing probable starter's identity, hand and announcement time, and no input in player_participation carries them; platoon is only a stand-in.
player_participation#pp_opp_starter_vint.catalog_action: Define an opposing-probable-starter input (identity, throwing hand, announcement timestamp) and attach it to the player_participation manager-decision stage.

player_participation#pp_postseason_regim.description: Both single-game start samples are Oct 14 2026 playoff games, but the rest-day and clinch-rest constructs are regular-season ones; in October stars rarely sit, rosters are round-specific and off days change pitching plans, so the manager-decision stage may not transfer.
player_participation#pp_postseason_regim.what_would_resolve: Fit start probabilities separately for postseason games or add a round/roster-eligibility input and test it.
player_participation#pp_postseason_regim.classification_rationale: Missing input: sampled start markets are postseason games where round-specific roster eligibility gates who can start, yet the manager-decision stage has only regular-season rest-day constructs.
player_participation#pp_postseason_regim.catalog_action: Author a postseason round and active-roster-eligibility input for player_participation and specify a separate postseason branch of the manager-decision stage.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_electorate.description: The electorate per award is not sourced: Reliever of the Year voting by retired relievers, and the Hank Aaron, Comeback Player and Executive of the Year electorates, are stated from memory, so the claim that one Plackett-Luce model serves all awards with shared coefficients is unsupported.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_electorate.what_would_resolve: Each awarding body's published voting procedure and historical ballots by award.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_electorate.classification_rationale: Verified electorates differ: Rivera/Hoffman by a six-reliever panel, Hank Aaron by Hall of Fame panel plus fan vote, Comeback by 30 MLB.com beat reporters. One shared Plackett-Luce model is wrong; inputs differ (fan-vote term).
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_electorate.catalog_action: Split season_leaders_and_awards award models by electorate: add fan-vote input for Hank Aaron, panel/beat-writer models for Reliever and Comeback, citing each body's procedure.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_eoty_elect.description: KXMLBEOTY (moved here from offfield_markets) names only 'the Governing League'; the electorate of the executive award (club executives versus writers or a media outlet) is unverified, so whether the BBWAA-style rank model, public ballots and the manager-centric wins-over-expectation input apply is unknown (carried from off_eoty_electorate).
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_eoty_elect.what_would_resolve: Identify the award Kalshi settles on and its electorate and ballot format.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_eoty_elect.classification_rationale: Verified: MLB Executive of the Year is voted by executives of all 30 clubs at the start of the postseason, with no public ballots, so the BBWAA-style rank model, public-ballot and manager win-over-expectation inputs do not apply.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_eoty_elect.catalog_action: Rewrite KXMLBEOTY inputs in season_leaders_and_awards: executive-voter model on front-office/team-improvement signals, removing public-ballot and manager inputs.

season_leaders_and_awards#lea_narrative_.description: Narrative (milestones, comeback, positional context) has no agreed quantitative measure and is hard to tag consistently; its effect size beyond WAR and team success may be small.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_narrative_.what_would_resolve: Define narrative flags (milestone, comeback, first-year, position) and test their incremental effect on vote share.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_narrative_.classification_rationale: Missing definition: narrative is listed as an award-vote driver but has no operational measure or tagging rule, so the input cannot be computed at all; the effect-size part is secondary.
season_leaders_and_awards#lea_narrative_.catalog_action: Define narrative flags (milestone, comeback, first-year, position scarcity) with tagging rules and sources as a concrete input of the award vote-share models.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_kxmlb.description: KXMLBSTAT is a generic season-stat series and only KXMLBSTAT-26P107-AP was sampled, so which other KXMLBSTAT markets exist, and whether they settle on non-velocity stats, is unknown; the archetype applies only to velocity markets.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_kxmlb.what_would_resolve: List every KXMLBSTAT market ticker and its rules text; route non-velocity markets to a separate archetype.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_kxmlb.classification_rationale: Series mapping defect: KXMLBSTAT is a generic season-stat series and only one velocity market was sampled; non-velocity KXMLBSTAT markets would be mis-routed to the velocity archetype.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_kxmlb.catalog_action: List every KXMLBSTAT ticker in the series ledger, keep velocity markets in pitch_velocity_extremes and route other stat markets to an archetype with suitable inputs.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.description: Five series with three mechanisms remain in one unregistered archetype (postseason league counts, player home-run exposure markets, a pitcher scoreless streak); one input list serves none of them fully, and the streak market has no other natural home.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Split the bucket into postseason-count, player-exposure and streak families with their own catalog entries.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.classification_rationale: Archetype mapping defect: five series with three mechanisms (postseason league counts, player HR exposure, scoreless streak) share one input list that serves none fully.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.catalog_action: Split player_and_team_counting_specials into postseason-count, player-exposure and scoreless-streak archetypes, each with its own mechanism and input list.
